title.narrative: Africa Regional Scholarship and Innovation Fund for Applied Sciences, Engineering and Technology

description.narrative: The objective of the Africa Regional Scholarship and Innovation Fund for Applied Sciences, Engineering and Technology Project is to strengthen the institutional capacity for quality and sustainable doctoral training, research and innovation in transformative technologies in sub-Saharan Africa. There are two components to the project, the first component being capacity development for the operation and management of the scholarship, research and innovation fund. This component will support strengthening of the RCU to become a scientific, technological and innovation capacity builder for PhD programs and universities in SSA in the fields of applied sciences and engineering that support transformative technologies, to make it capable of operating and growing RSIF efficiently and sustainably. This component includes four subcomponents: capacity building for managing and growing the RSIF general fund and setting up a RSIF permanent fund, capacity development for the operation and management of doctoral training scholarships in selected African universities and research grants in ASET fields, capacity development for improving quality of PhD programs and research in ASET fields, and capacity development for the operation and management of innovation grants. The second component is the Scholarships and Research Grants for ASET. This component, financed by a US$9 million22 contribution from the Government of Korea administered by the Bank, will provide financing for scholarships and research grants in ASET fields in Sub-Saharan Africa. SSA countries have shown interest in contributing funds to RSIF either through their own resources or through national/regional IDA credit. Some of these contributions may also be channeled through regional IDA projects, for instance the third ACE, which is currently under preparation. This component includes two subcomponents: doctoral training in ASET fields in selected SSA host Universities and international partner universities, and research grants.
To strengthen the institutional capacity for quality doctoral training, research, and innovation in transformative technologies in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA).

title.narrative: Number of research papers submitted by staff members or scholars supported by the project for publication to internationally indexed journals

comment.narrative: A total of 323 high-quality peer-reviewed scientific papers have been published by staff members/faculty, scholars, and grantees, 108 of which were authored by women. Of the 323 publications, 297 are by Scholars and 44 by Grantees (of the 44 Grantees publications, 18 are co-authored by Scholars who are involved in the funded research grants projects and 5 are from AGriDI project). Cohort 1 has published 63 peer-reviewed and conference papers, while Cohort 2, 3 and 4 have published 132, 68 and 31 papers, respectively, and 1 paper is co-authored by Cohort 1 and 3 scholars, and 2 papers co-authored by cohort 3 and 4 scholars. The 323 total publications have been cited 1,747 times (self-citations excluded), 335,432 full-text views (downloads), 289,487 abstract views with 0 â€“ 19.3 journal impact factor range. icipe continues to support Rsif scholars and faculty at AHUs to write high-quality articles, and publication of the articles in relevant international journals.

title.narrative: Number of RSIF host institutions that start the international accreditation process at the PhD program level or at the institution level

comment.narrative: During the restructuring in December 2021, the indicator was adjusted to measure the â€œstartâ€ of the international accreditation process, which implies that the RSIF institution has identified an international accreditation agency, signed a contract with the agency and completed self-evaluation for the accreditation process. Accordingly, the RCU conducted an assessment of the accreditation of the target programs at AHUs and developed an action plan to support the AHUs to initiate and attain the required accreditation. The required support for accreditation is incorporated into the overall capacity-building strategy for AHUs, and implementation of the action plan is ongoing. So far, seven (7) AHUs have either started or completed the accreditation process, with support from the ACE Impact projects. The RCU hired a consultant in February 2024 to assist the remaining 8 AHUs to start the accreditation process. The universities started the international accreditation processes: (1) African University of Science and Technology completed the process by HCERES, (2) University of Ghana started the process with AQAS), Germany, (3) University of Port Harcourt initiated the process with HCERES, (4) University of Rwanda initiated the process with ZEvA, (5) Bayero University initiated the process with HCERES, (6) UniversitA FAlix HouphouÃ«t-Boigny completed the process with HCERES. title.narrative: Percentage of RSIF scholars in Cohorts 1 and 2 employed/self-employed in their field of study at least 6 months after graduation (% of female graduates employed/self-employed).

comment.narrative: On track. This is a new indicator introduced during the project restructuring in December 2021, which reflects the percentage of students who had graduated and got employment six months after graduation to the total number of potential graduates in cohorts 1 and 2. Of the 15 Cohort 1 scholars (three female), 11 (two female) have completed their studies, and all 11 are employed. Among the 61 Cohort 2 scholars (27 female), 31 (10 female) had completed their studies as of December 2024. Of these, 18 (seven female) are employed as postdoctoral researchers, faculty members, or researchers in various institutions. This represents 38 percent (i.e., 29 graduates from Cohorts 1 and 2 who are employed or self-employed) out of the 76 scholars enrolled in these cohorts. The employment rate for female scholars in Cohorts 1 and 2, measured as the percentage employed within at least six months of graduation, is 30 percent (i.e., 9 out of 30 enrolled female scholars).

title.narrative: Percentage of RSIF scholars in Cohorts 1 and 2 employed/self-employed in their field of study at least 6 months after graduation (% of female graduates employed/self-employed).

comment.narrative: This is a new indicator introduced during the project restructuring in December 2021. Of the 15 cohort 1 scholars, 11 have completed, one (1) is the Director of the Microbiology Unit at the National Reference Laboratory in Rwanda, 7 are employed as faculty in different AHUs, two (2) are part time lecturers, and one (1) scholar recently got a Post Doc position at KU Leuven in Belgium after unsuccessfully pursuing a faculty position at the University of Rwanda. Of the 11 cohort 1 scholars who have completed, two (2) are female. One (1) cohort 2 female scholar completed her studies in August 2023. Eigteen (18) Cohort 2 scholars completed their studies between April and August 2024, and eight (8) of them are employed as Post Docs, faculty members or researchers in various institutions. Out of these 18 scholars, six (6 ) are female and three (3) are employed. The other 43 active cohort 2 scholars are still ongoing with their studies.

title.narrative: Level of satisfaction of RSIF Scholars with the quality of the learning environment and delivery of the target doctoral programs at the AHUs.

comment.narrative: Target achieved. This is a new indicator introduced during the project restructuring in December 2021. The level of satisfaction by RSIF scholars is assessed by the quality of the doctoral content, curriculum/training delivery, faculty/staff, and teaching and learning facilities. This figure was derived from the 2024 RSIF studentsâ€™ satisfaction survey. It is based on a 5-point Likert scale (1=very unsatisfied, 2=unsatisfied, 3=Neutral, 4=Satisfied, 5=Very Satisfied), this is the percentage of enrolled students who respond to being at the 4 and 5 Likert scale rating.

title.narrative: Level of satisfaction of RSIF Scholars with the quality of the learning environment and delivery of the target doctoral programs at the AHUs.

comment.narrative:
This is a new indicator introduced during the project restructuring in December 2021. The level of satisfaction by RSIF scholars is assessed by the quality of the doctoral content, curriculum/training delivery, faculty/staff, and teaching and learning facilities. Based on a 5-point Likert scale (1=very unsatisfied, 2=unsatisfied, 3=Neutral, 4=Satisfied, 5=Very Satisfied), this is the percentage of enrolled students who respond to being at the 4 and 5 Likert scale rating.
The latest project stakeholder satisfaction survey was conducted in November 2023 and received responses from 184 fully enrolled students (63 female and 121 male); 3 from the first cohort, 41 from the second cohort, 58 from the third cohort, and 82 from the fourth cohort. The next round of satisfaction surveys for general RSIF scholars will be launched in November 2024.

title.narrative: Set up a foundation for establishment of the permanent fund.

comment.narrative: Target achieved. This is a new indicator introduced during the project restructuring in December 2021. The definition of the indicator for the foundation for the establishment of the permanent fund included a comprehensive feasibility study conducted, a financial model, an implementation plan, a funding strategy, a draft board charter, an investment policy, and fund manager TORs. These documents are completed and an Advisory Committee was proposed. Ideas for RSIF permanent fund by Ai2 Advisory of a Carbon X Green and Venture Capital Fund were presented to the PASET CAG and EB on February 1, 2023, in Kigali, Rwanda, and was deemed to require further study on the viability of carbon financing. So far, in collaboration with the PASET structures, icipe is exploring financial models, and a 6th PASET Forum with a focus on resource mobilization was held on 23-15 April 2024 in Nairobi, Kenya, and a Governing Council meeting was conducted in February 28, 2025.

title.narrative: Set up a foundation for establishment of the permanent fund.

comment.narrative: This is a new indicator introduced during the project restructuring in December 2021. The definition of the indicator for the foundation for the establishment of the permanent fund included a comprehensive feasibility study conducted, a financial model, an implementation plan, a funding strategy, a draft board charter, an investment policy, and fund manager TORs. These documents are completed and an Advisory Committee was proposed. Ideas for RSIF permanent fund by Ai2 Advisory of a Carbon X Green and Venture Capital Fund were presented to the PASET CAG and EB on February 1, 2023, in Kigali, Rwanda. It was decided that the ideas were very early stage and needed further study of the viability of using carbon financing models. So far, in collaboration with the PASET structures, icipe is exploring financial models, and a CAG sub-committee is in place to explore resource mobilizations, the PASET Strategy 2024-2034 is completed, and a 6th PASET Forum and RSIF Annual Conference was held on 23-15 April 2024 in Nairobi, Kenya with a focus on resource mobilization.
